status_rationale: Absolute per-profile floors are recorded from the initial bound-revision baseline for honest later comparison. They remain explicitly provisional until a reviewed ratification. They must not be lowered in the same change that fails them, and they must not be treated as release gates until status becomes 'reviewed'.

bound_revision_policy.note: A changed revision invalidates historical findings and requires a fresh baseline; it is not automatically a failure.

rules.statement: Comparisons require exact match on hardware class, OS family/version class, Python version, dependency digest, repository revision, dataset id, seed, concurrency, durability mode, warmup count, sample count, confidence level, resource profile, workload id, path_class, and ack_state.
Primary transaction throughput is committed_tps. accepted_tps may be reported alongside but must never satisfy a committed floor or regression gate.
cold, warm, and cache path results are incomparable across classes. Cache/index speedups are reported separately from cold correctness paths.
Default regression gate: no more than 5% throughput regression versus the pinned accepted baseline unless an approved variance receipt explains it.
Default regression gate: no more than 10% p99 latency regression versus the pinned accepted baseline unless an approved variance receipt explains it.
After floors are reviewed, absolute per-profile floors cannot be lowered in the same change that fails them.
While status is provisional, floors are diagnostic anchors for comparison and must not be enforced as release failures solely by absolute magnitude.
Benchmark errors or partial sample sets cannot pass a comparison gate.
No durability, authorization, consistency, or correctness relaxation may accompany a performance claim.
Metrics must have bounded cardinality and must not embed secrets, tokens, or absolute home paths.

observation_anchors.description: Non-numeric observations captured at the bound revision. These are diagnostics, not performance floors.

root_eager_imports.summary: Root package import initializes JIT manager and backend_config helpers; binary auto-download is gated but import surface remains broad.

mcp_eager_imports.summary: MCP++ server module eagerly imports anyio, mcplusplus, and HierarchicalToolManager; constructor references EventDAGStore without a local import (confirmed baseline blocker).

runtime_metadata_version_mismatch.summary: ipfs_kit_py.__version__ disagrees with pyproject.toml / setup.py project version at the bound revision.

dependency_projection_drift.summary: Runtime dependency projection (importable distribution versions) may drift from declared pyproject dependencies and optional extras; baseline records both digests.

transaction_specific_slo.summary: No transaction-specific SLO is defined at the bound revision. KITA-004 establishes measurement identity only; RuntimeSLO@1 is owned by a later harness task.

metadata_txn.note: Numeric floor deferred until first full baseline run is reviewed; identity and metric names are pinned.

small_object_txn.note: Numeric floor deferred until first full baseline run is reviewed; identity and metric names are pinned.

mixed_vfs.note: Numeric floor deferred until first full baseline run is reviewed.

wal_commit.note: Must use committed durability metrics only.

cold_import_root.note: Import budgets provisional; cold path only.

cold_import_mcp.note: Import budgets provisional; cold path only.

resource_ceilings.note: Resource ceilings provisional until soak evidence exists.

committed_tps.description: Completed transactions that survived the declared durability protocol.

accepted_tps.description: Accepted but not necessarily durable transactions. Diagnostic only for transaction floors.
